call1_AB.raw:
Both fortunes carry the cookie voice and the loss. A's joke — the exchange "keeping it safe" — is a solid jab at frozen funds, and the "until you can laugh about this" gives it warmth, but the punchline arrives a little late and explains itself. B opens with a perfect classic cookie formula ("You will soon meet a wealthy stranger") and then detonates it: the stranger is the trader's own pre-liquidation self. It names the loss directly, lands rueful rather than cruel, reads whole in one breath at 11 words, and the last word is the surprise. It also keeps the oracular register longer before breaking it, which is exactly what criterion 5 rewards.

A is funny; B is a fortune cookie that happens to be funny.

Verdict: B, margin 2.
call1_AB.reasoning_tail:
Compare A and B.

A: "Your future holds great wealth — the exchange is keeping it safe until you can laugh about this." Cookie voice, oracle-ish, loss in it (exchange keeping it safe — implies funds gone/withdrawals halted), trader loss. Warm, rueful, decent. ~19 words? "Your(1) future(2) holds(3) great(4) wealth(5) the(6) exchange(7) is(8) keeping(9) it(10) safe(11) until(12) you(13) can(14) laugh(15) about(16) this(17)" — 17 words. Good.

B: "You will soon meet a wealthy stranger: yourself, before the liquidation." Fortune voice (meeting a stranger — classic cookie trope), liquidation explicit, surprising turn. 11 words. Very fresh, double meaning, rueful and warm-ish. Joke lands on loss directly.

Both strong. Criterion 1: both have trader loss + cookie voice. B explicitly names liquidation; A implies it via exchange. Criterion 2: both laugh not cry. Criterion 3: both fine. Criterion 4: fresh — B uses classic fortune "meet a stranger" twist; A's twist is exchange holding funds (also good, slightly more obvious withdrawal-halt joke?). B's twist feels fresher and reads whole in a breath. Criterion 5: B keeps oracle voice better ("You will soon meet...") then breaks it.

Pick B, margin 2-3. I'd say 2.

call2_BA.raw:
Both carry the loss and the voice, so the tie-breakers decide. A's twist — the wealthy stranger being your past self — is rueful but it's the move anyone reaches for first, and it edges toward melancholy rather than a laugh. B works harder: "the exchange is keeping it safe" lands the double meaning (safe = gone, in custody, forever) and the last clause turns it warm — you will laugh again, just not rich. It reads whole in one breath, breaks the oracular voice at the right moment, and makes the trader laugh at the loss instead of sighing at it.

Verdict: B, margin 2.
call2_BA.reasoning_tail:
A: "wealthy stranger: yourself, before the liquidation" — fortune voice, twist, rueful, loss named, trader implied. Fresh, funny.

B: fortune voice, "exchange keeping it safe" — double meaning of "safe" (custody risk), loss implied, laugh about it. Also good. Which is funnier? B's joke: exchange holding funds = they took your money, plus "laugh about this" acknowledges loss. A's twist is the classic "your past self was rich" — poignant. B has the extra "until you can laugh about this" which adds warmth and rue, and "safe" does double duty (kept safe = never returned). Word counts: A = 12 words. B = 18 words.

Criterion 4: fresh turn. A's turn is decent but "yourself before liquidation" is a fairly obvious move. B's double meaning of "safe" plus the laugh line is fresher. I'll pick B, margin 2.
